title: Engineering
description: How Lathe's code and its history are kept, so every change reads the same way to the Agent who makes it and the Owner who reviews and releases it.

title: Experience
description: The qualities every use case keeps for the people who read and work in Lathe, whatever their goal: views that hold still and stay smooth, every command by keyboard and assistive technology with its keys shown where it is used, a phone that reads the spec, and, on a Mac, an app that behaves as a Mac app does. They were use cases once; they are qualities, not goals (LA-STD-MODELING-R15).

title: Domain modeling
description: How the domain models Lathe writes are shaped, its own and every product's, where the checks hold them to it.

title: Naming
description: How the records Lathe writes are named and worded, its own and every product's, where the checks hold them to it: titles, names, goals, happenings, statements and the text each kind keeps.

title: Lathe's principles
description: The principles every part of Lathe follows, and every product it models: from mistake-proofing (poka-yoke) and standard work, mistakes are refused when they are made, each thing has one way, no rule has an exception, and a standard that proves wrong is changed everywhere at once; and essential complexity is decided once, per product, while accidental complexity is derived, provided or a recorded fill at a slot.

title: Traceability
description: The bar Lathe's own spec holds on main: every obligation designed, built and proved, and nothing for the check to report.
